text:
One of the central aims of education is to help students become independent learners. Artificial intelligence can support this goal by providing explanations, feedback, and access to information beyond the classroom. However, it can also weaken independence when students become dependent on automated guidance for every stage of learning.

AI can encourage independence by allowing students to seek help without waiting for a teacher. A learner who does not understand a concept can request another explanation, ask for an example, or practise with additional questions. This immediate support may reduce frustration and help students continue studying on their own.

AI can also assist with planning. Students may use digital tools to organise revision schedules, identify weak areas, and set learning goals. Such support can be especially valuable for students who struggle with time management or do not have access to private tutoring.

Nevertheless, independence does not simply mean completing work without a teacher. It also involves making decisions, tolerating uncertainty, and evaluating one’s own understanding. If students rely on AI to choose topics, generate arguments, organise paragraphs, and correct every mistake, they may complete tasks without developing these abilities.

A further concern is that students may confuse assistance with understanding. An AI-generated explanation may appear clear, but genuine learning requires the student to apply the idea independently. Teachers should therefore include tasks that require students to explain concepts in their own words, solve unfamiliar problems, and reflect on how they used AI.

AI can strengthen student independence when it provides timely support while preserving personal responsibility. It becomes harmful when it replaces judgement, effort, and self-correction. Educational institutions should teach students to use AI as a temporary guide rather than a permanent substitute for independent thought.
